sustained_decode.prompt: Explain why hash-table lookup is usually constant time but can take linear time in the worst case. Use three concise sentences.

message.content: Hash-table lookup is usually O(1) because a hash function maps each key to a bucket, allowing direct access without scanning other elements. However, if many keys hash to the same bucket (a collision), the table must search through that bucket's entries, which can grow to contain all n elements. In the worst case—such as a poor hash function or adversarial keys—all elements collide into one bucket, degrading lookup to O(n).
